title: Operations
summary: Production runbook for the research-agent service: container and Fly.io deployment, the SQLite-to-Postgres migration, CI gates, configuration knobs, and project layout.
scope: CI pipeline (ruff, 364 tests, 12 offline eval cases, image build, smoke test)
cost accounting and spend caps (AGENT_MAX_RUN_COST_USD, DEMO_DAILY_USD_CAP)
notes: Primary structure is a prose runbook (deployment procedures, migration steps, CI description), which the taxonomy places under DOC. Competing SPEC signal: two substantive contract tables (code knobs and environment variables with exact defaults) plus hard operational invariants. Resolved to DOC because no section defines an API, schema, or SLO; the tables document existing defaults rather than mandate them. Synthesizer should still lift these as operational constraints: min_machines_running = 1 while SQLite is the backend (single writer, per-machine volume, second machine 404s on existing sessions); volume required at /data or memory silently no-ops; container listens on port 8000; credentials must never enter an image layer and /health reports presence only; CI runs every gate with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""; pgvector guard test must fail rather than skip; deploys run through Fly's GitHub integration and are NOT gated on CI, so a direct push to main can deploy failing code; Fly Launch PRs must not be merged (they have twice broken the deploy, once silently via internal_port 8080); default per-run spend cap $1.00, rolling 24h demo cap $5.00, 10 requests per visitor IP per hour; switching backends does not migrate data; VECTOR_DIMENSIONS 1024 for voyage-3.5.
